newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Supreme Court to rule on assisted-suicide ban.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Supreme Court to rule on assisted-suicide ban.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court said on Tuesday it would decide whether mentally competent, terminally ill patients have the legal right to seek help from their doctors to commit suicide.
The nation's highest court agreed to take up the highly emotional question of whether states may ban doctor-assisted suicide, an issue which has sparked a fierce national debate.

It will be one of the most important and closely watched controversies the nine justices will decide during the 1996-97 term, which opens on Monday. The ruling could have a broad impact as more than 30 U.S. states have made assisted suicide a crime.
The high court's action to review laws from New York and Washington states banning physician-assisted suicide sets the stage for a possible landmark decision before July.

The justices in a pair of brief orders said they would hear appeals by New York and Washington states of two precedent-setting rulings that struck down as unconstitutional laws that make it a crime for physicians to assist in a suicide.

The case before the Supreme Court does not involve Dr. Jack Kevorkian, a retired pathologist and the nation's best known advocate of assisted suicide who has publicly acknowledged attending more than 40 deaths since 1990.
